newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian drug abuse booms but lower than in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug abuse booms but lower than in U.S.

text.p: Drug consumption in Colombia has doubled in the last four years but is still lower than in the United States, a government-funded study said on Tuesday.
Researcher Edgar Rodriguez said about 400,000 Colombians have used illegal narcotics at least once in their lives, a small percentage of the country's population.
But he warned that drug use in Colombia, the world's largest producer of cocaine, could easily soar.

"At any moment consumption could take off. Colombia is a seedbed for consumption and we must take great care to control the situation," Rodriguez, head of research at the Fundacion Santa Fe private health foundation, told a press conference.

Rodriguez said 1.8 percent of all Colombians aged between 12 and 60 years old had used drugs in the last year, double the rate for 1992. Recent U.S. studies revealed that 10.7 percent of Americans in the same age bracket had used some form of illicit substance in the last year, he added.
